The North Quays main contract works are progressing well.  For the Sustainable 
Transport Bridge the concrete infi ll stage for the fi rst cofferdam (gridline E) is 
complete and the process for dewatering the second cofferdams (gridline D) is 
progressing.  
Images of the South Quays Plaza site illustrate sheet piling at the Quay wall that 
will form the southern landing point for the Sustainable Transport bridge and 
cofferdams within the river that will support the bridge. 
The image shows the foundations for the new train station and platforms, and the 
reinforced concrete walls for the station building are underway and visible. Sheet 
piling is illustrated in the image above for the retaining walls to the rear of the 
Bus Eireann site (S25) in anticipation of the new road layout at the Abbey Road / 
Fountain Street junction.  
The completed car parking area within Our Lady of Good Council National School 
can be seen in the distance.  The bridge abutments for the western access bridge 
(S19) are also well advanced and visible from Dock Road. This is an image of the 
pump station works currently under construction by David Walsh Civil Engineer-
ing, works are over 80% complete.
Traffi c management measures are in place along Dock Road to install sewer and 
surface water network services.  Works and associated traffi c management is 
advancing westwards in December, necessitating minor amendments to the traffi c 
management.  These works will relocate to the Abbey Road / Fountain Street 
junction in the new year.

RURAL TOURISM 
Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme (ORIS) 
€100,000 in Outdoor Recreation Funding Announced for Waterford
On Tuesday, November 21st, Minister for Rural and Community Development, Heather Humphreys announced funding 
of almost €2.3 million nationally to support the development of 50 outdoor adventure projects across Ireland. The in-
vestment under the Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme (ORIS) will be key to enhancing outdoor amenities such 
as our walkways, cycleways, rivers, lakes and beaches.As part of this announcement two Waterford projects received 
a very welcome funding boost; Blackwater River Valley Outdoor Recreation Plan and Comeragh Mountains Outdoor 
Recreation Management Plan. The Project Development Measures will fund the preparatory work required to bring large 
scale outdoor recreation projects to a shovel-ready stage. Each project will receive €50,000 in funding under this round 
of ORIS funding with a minimum of a further 10% in funding being contributed by Waterford City and County Council. It 
is envisaged that the projects will be implemented in 2024.
Currently implementing 15 projects around the county, funded under the Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme 
(ORIS) between 2020 and 2022

TOURISM 
The most recent Waterford Rural Tourism Networking Event held in The Park Hotel Dungarvan on Wednesday 22nd of 
November was a great success. With over 50 businesses from all five cluster areas; Copper Coast, Blackwater Valley, 
Comeragh Uplands, Gaeltacht, and Waterford Estuary in attendance. The event was a fantastic opportunity for busi-
nesses to talk, connect, and plan how they might work together to create better visitor experiences across Waterford. 
Fáilte Ireland, Waterford City and County Council and Waterford LEADER Partnership provided updates and highlighted 
the supports available for the Waterford Rural Tourism Network to develop, as well as potential funding opportunities. 
The Rural Tourism Network will continue to grow and develop in 2024.
The next Economic Development & Enterprise SPC is scheduled for February 2024.

ARCHIVES AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT 
ARCHIVES
Diverse Waterford Project -Open Call to Elected Members
The Archives in collaboration with the Library Service has created an Oral History Project- Diverse Waterford funded by 
Creative Waterford. We would like to record elected members about their experiences as elected representatives and 
ensure that we have an oral history record of elected members to accompany our written records. If any elected 
members would like to participate then please contact the Archivist at archivist@waterfordcouncil.ie 
The project also aims to facilitate Community Groups to carry out Oral History recordings which can then be stored 
in the Archive and shared through the Diverse Waterford website. In addition to advice and guidance available on the 
website for groups the project also has sound recording equipment available to loan to interested community groups. If 
members know of any community groups that would be interested in participating in the project please contact 
archivist@waterfordcouncil.ie  
In November staff in the Library Service and the Archives Service received training on editing snippets of the recordings 
made to date so that these can be shared on SoundCloud. You can access the snippets that have been created to date 
on our website www.diversewaterford.ie 
Training has previously been provided in Waterford City and in Dungarvan for Community Groups and this training will 
again be made available in 2024.

Derelict Sites
The Derelict sites team are currently dealing with 260 properties that are considered either derelict or potentially 
derelict. The activity in recent months has substantially increased with 77 derelict properties identifi ed and on the 
Derelict Sites Register. Initial engagement with owners or their representatives is key to resolution of the issues of 
dereliction and to understand the various reasons why the properties are in a derelict stage. 
The level of activity in the property market for vacant and derelict properties has increased and of the properties we 
have identifi ed as derelict, a number of them have been brought to the market and some are at ‘to let’/ ‘sale agreed’ 
stage. We continue the engagement with the new owners of those properties to ensure they are aware of their 
responsibilities under the Derelict Sites Act, 1990. Due to the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant, there is a 
noticeable increase in the number of derelict and vacant properties on the market at the current time.

Heritage Officer Report 
Community Monuments Fund- All Districts
Four projects were awarded funding under the Community Monuments Fund allocated by the National Monuments 
Service of the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage to a value of €270,000 for conservation and 
survey of a range of archaeological sites across the city and county and works have now been completed. 
The Community Monuments Fund 2024 is open for applications until February 14th 2023. Grants up to €100,000 are 
available for essential repairs and capital works for the conservation of archaeological monuments. Grants of up to 
€30,000 are available for Conservation Management Plans aimed at identifying measures for conservation of 
archaeological monuments and improving public access.  All proposals should be able to illustrate some tangible public 
value benefit. This may include access, physical and virtual, or provision of information to the public.
Woodstown Viking Site-Waterford Metro
Archaeologists from the Discovery Programme completed a geo-physical survey of the Woodstown Viking Site in early 
October. A delegation from Stavanger Museum in Norway visited Waterford   on November 10th taking in City Hall, the 
Viking Triangle, Waterford Museums and the Woodstown Viking site.
Biodiversity Funding 
Funding under the NPWS Local Biodiversity Action Plan Fund was used to satellite tag a number of Brent Geese earlier 
in 2023 and the project has been filmed by a TV company for RTE Junior which will be aired in autumn 2024. The series 
will feature the Dungarvan Brent Geese and pupils from St. Mary’s National School and trace the tagged geese on their 
journey to Iceland Arctic Canada.
Biodiversity Officer 
Waterford City and County Council are partaking in the Heritage Council supported Biodiversity Officer Programme and 
a Biodiversity Officer will be in post in the local authority in early 2024.

Seirbhísí Pobail / Community Services
RURAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME:
The current LEADER programme is at an end. The LAG has allocated €7,917,335 to 171 projects since 2017. Three 
decommitments totalling just over €15,000 will occur. Two projects will run into 2024.The budget for the new LEADER 
Programme 2023 to 2029 is €6.1m with €4.5m allocated to projects. Supplementary funds may be allocated over the 
course of the programme which be most welcome given the emerging challenges in rural areas. The Local Development 
strategy has been approved by the department and contract signing is imminent.
COMHAIRLE NA NÓG:
The topic for 2024 has been identified by the young people and this will now be the basis for work in the coming year. 
The Podcast series on the young peoples chosen topic is fully complete and published. The AGM took place in November 
in the Tower Hotel, Waterford with a huge attendance.  The young people continue to participate in their nominated local 
and national committees. 
WATERFORD AGE FRIENDLY PROGRAMME:
Delivery of the year 1 action plan has begun with six of the seven Implementation Subgroups (the majority having met 
multiple times). The remaining group will have initial meeting in early December. The new Age Friendly Alliance is due to 
have its initial meeting during during early December.
WELL WATERFORD (LCDC SUB-GROUP)
The Well Waterford committee and implementing partners have several meetings and events arranged to bring about a 
localised approach to community wellbeing and development. Municipal District meetings took place for elected mem-
bers and our implementing partners to meet and input into the Well Waterford structure. One of the key actions from 
these meetings was to organise a combined approach in meeting people in the community. So for we have contributed 
to meeting to develop a “connecting communities” roadshow for quarter one of next year. We will be hosting information 
sessions for the Municipal districts in January and February. With the following dates identified for a 10am start.  This will 
be an opportunity for elected member to contriubute to actions for 2024 as part of the Healthy Waterford planning process. 
Further information will be sent in due course.

UKRAINIAN COMMUNITY RESPONSE FORUM:
The Ukrainian CRF is in place to assist with housing, supporting and integrating Ukrainian refugees into our commu-
nities.   All key agencies are working in collaboration to provide services and supports to all Ukrainians arriving into 
Waterford.  Approximately 2,734 Ukrainian refugees have been registered in Waterford to date with over 1,983 Ukraini-
ans having been received directly into Waterford Council run Rest Centres in Dungarvan and Waterford City.  To date 
1,469 have been matched with pledged and other accommodation sourced by Waterford Council.   Over 90% of expiring 
licence agreements are being renewed and the team continue to work on supporting pledge owners and occupiers here 
in Waterford.  Waterford Area Partnership are supporting all Ukrainians with integration into our communities. 
The  ‘offer a home’ pledge call for vacant properties is still open with over 245 Ukrainians being accommodated in 
pledged accommodation  to date.  
Any queries on same should be directed to offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie or 058 22059. 
COMMUNITY SAFETY INNOVATION FUND PROJECTS:
Preparatory work has commenced for the in two successful 2023 Grant Applications to the Community Safety Innovation 
Fund, Consent Matters and A Community Safety Warden Initiative for Waterford City. These will be advanced rapidly in 
January 2024.
LCSP SMALL GRANT FUND
Twenty five applicant were informed that they were successful in The Department of Justice Waterford Community Safety 
Partnership Small Grants Fund to deliver innovative projects and initiatives that respond to the needs identified in the 
WLCSP Community Safety Plan 2023-2028. 
Amounts approved by the WLCSP Steering Committee range between €1,000 to €5,000 and a listing will be circulated 
shortly
WLCSP MEETINGS:
The Education, Training & Awareness and Building Community Capacity Working Group held it’s most recent meeting on 
the 30th November 2023 in person and the Reducing Criminality and Safe Environment & Infrastructure Working Group 
held theirs by zoom on 16th November 2023. 
The next WLCSP Plenary Meeting is scheduled for 4th December at 630pm in the Civic Offices, Dungarvan.

Climate Action Plan
The consultation on the Climate Action Plan opened on 1st 
November and will remain open until 15th December. The public can access the document on the consult portal. To date 
there have been 4 submissions. To encourage engagement with the plan we are hosting events across the country in 
libraries and in communities. Community groups are hosting us. See below for locations. These events are about the 
Climate Action Plan and about giving the public advice on energy saving.

ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION & AWARENESS
Environmental Education & Awareness
The Tom Murphy Litter Competition for Secondary Schools has been completed and judged. 15 secondary schools 
across Waterford city and county entered the competition and received litter pickers, high visibility vests, gloves and 
bags to allow them to carry out litter picks of their designated area. Over a six week period, schools have been carrying 
out regular clean ups, with many schools embracing the competition fully, carrying out multiple clean ups each week 
with different classes. We have been in regular contact with each school and photos of these clean-ups were posted on 
social media.  A prizegiving and presentation of certificates of participation will take place in the Mayors Parlour in early 
December, with all schools being presented with certificates of participation and the winning schools being awarded with 
a prize of €1,500 sponsored by Tom Murphy Car Sales. 
Climate Change Secondary Schools Conference
The Environmental Awareness Officer took part in the organisation and running of a Climate Action Conference for 
secondary schools with the Climate Action Team during October. A presentation was also given on the day on the topic 
of Sustainability and Resources. 
Green Schools Visits
Green Schools visits are underway, with some schools requesting advice on their current theme in the programme or 
help with their work while others are availing of an early assessment visit to their school. Waterpark College raised their 
first Green Flag at a ceremony in November.

Picker Pals Programme
35 Waterford primary schools are participating in the Picker Pals litter programme once again this school year. This 
programme is most suitable for 1st and 2nd class children but has classes participating from 3rd, 4th and 5th class also. 
It teaches about litter and involves activity based learning to promote a keen sense of responsibility for the environment. 
Students take part in online and in class learning about litter as well as carrying out a local clean up with parents etc. 
each weekend
Composting for Schools Programme
The 8 Secondary Schools taking part in the Composting for Schools programme have received their initial visit. The 
main purpose of this visit was to carry out a waste audit to help schools to prevent, reduce and reuse their waste with 
a strong focus on recycling food waste. Schools have also taken part in 5 online sessions to learn more about waste 
prevention, recycling and composting within a school. The next step is for them to complete a brief action plan to tackle 
waste within their school. There will then be staff and student training in each school in the New Year.
Anti-Dog Fouling Campaign
A recent campaign reminded dog owners of the need to clean up their dog’s waste by bagging it and binning it. A press 
release and social media posts were used to prompt dog owners to pick up their dog waste and place it into a bin, 
instead of leaving it on the ground, or leaving the bag on a tree, fence, etc. It also reiterated the health impacts and other 
consequences that dog fouling can have.
Blue Flag/Green Coast
The Green Coast Award is a symbol of environmental excellence and has been established to acknowledge, promote 
and protect the environment of our beaches. All sites must be managed in partnership with the local community to be 
considered for the Green Coast Award. The award encourages community involvement through the setting up of Clean 
Coasts Groups. Clean Coasts group formulate their own aims, objectives and activities to clean up and protect their 
adopted stretch of coastline. The Environmental Awareness Officer is currently working on the applications for the 7 
Green Coast locations and 3 Blue Flags for beaches, largely in relation to the community element of the application i.e. 
work and activities carried out with local groups, schools and wider community. In order to qualify for the Blue Flag 
Award, a series of rigorous environmental, educational, safety-related and access-related criteria must be met and 
maintained.
Community Clean-Ups
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally 
dumped waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. The Environment De-
partment continue to supply bags, gloves and litter pickers from both Dungarvan and Waterford offices to many of the 
groups taking part, as well as collecting the bags of  litter afterwards.
